fullPassage:
(A) Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer? We can work on some drills — just the two of us." Eva hesitated. "I don't know, Coach. I'm pretty tired." Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. "Just ten minutes. It'll be fun. I promise." Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed reluctant. They practiced passing the ball together.

(B) The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played. There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but led the team successfully. After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to remind you of that." Eva's face softened, as she realized she had been too hard on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is doing my best, not being perfect."

(C) Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. And you've always had plenty of that." Eva's gaze met Ms. Blake's. "Do you really think so?" Ms. Blake said firmly, "Yes. The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully.

(D) Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Breaking the silence, Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember." Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva.

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, ①<u>watching</u> Eva pack up her things. She paused, then called out. Eva ②<u>hesitated</u>. Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed ③<u>reluctantly</u>. They practiced ④<u>passing</u> the ball together.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Eva는 여전히 꺼리는(reluctant) 듯했다. ③ reluctantly(부사) → reluctant(형용사): seemed 뒤에 형용사 보어.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ reluctantly → reluctant: seemed(감각동사) 뒤에 주격보어로 형용사가 필요.
✅ ① watching: 분사구문(동시동작). 적절.
❌ ② hesitated: 과거형 동사. 적절.
❌ ④ passing: practiced + V-ing. 적절.
det.tip: 감각동사(seem/look/feel) + 형용사(보어). 부사(X). practice + V-ing

questions.passage: The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva ①<u>played</u>. There was a new confidence ②<u>that</u> hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but ③<u>leading</u> the team successfully. She said, "What matters ④<u>is</u> doing my best."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Eva는 득점하지는 못했지만 팀을 성공적으로 이끌었다(led). ③ leading → led: but으로 연결된 병렬 구조.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ leading → led: 'didn't score but led'에서 but 앞뒤 동사 병렬. leading(현재분사)은 불가.
✅ ① played: 과거 동사. 적절.
❌ ② that: 관계대명사 주격. 적절.
❌ ④ is: What matters(주어절)에 대한 단수 동사. 적절.
det.tip: 병렬 구조: didn't V but V(과거형). What matters is ~ = 중요한 것은 ~이다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a ①<u>reassuring</u> hand on Eva's shoulder. "Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion." Eva's gaze ②<u>met</u> Ms. Blake's. Ms. Blake said firmly, "The way you play, the energy you ③<u>bring</u> — that's ④<u>that</u> makes you special."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그것이 너를 특별하게 만드는 것(what)이다. ④ that → what: 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 필요.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ that → what: 'that's what makes you special'. that 뒤에 makes의 주어 역할을 하는 관계대명사 필요.
✅ ① reassuring: 현재분사(형용사). 적절.
❌ ② met: 과거 동사. 적절.
❌ ③ bring: 현재시제. 적절.
det.tip: that's what + V = 그것이 바로 ~하는 것이다. what = the thing that(선행사 포함)

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed ①<u>elsewhere</u>. ②<u>Breaking</u> the silence, Ms. Blake asked about last year's final game. Eva ③<u>recalled</u> the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still ④<u>were</u>," replied Ms. Blake.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "너는 여전히 잘해(are)." ④ were → are: 현재 시점에서 '여전히 잘한다'는 의미이므로 현재시제.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ were → are: 원문 'You still are'. 현재 상태를 나타내므로 are.
✅ ① elsewhere: 부사. 적절.
❌ ② Breaking: 분사구문. 적절.
❌ ③ recalled: 과거 동사. 적절.
det.tip: 시제 일치: 'I was good back then' → 'You still are (good now)'. 과거↔현재 구별

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field. Eva hesitated. Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile and said it would be fun. Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed reluctant. They practiced passing the ball together. Ms. Blake noticed Eva's movements were slow and her __________ seemed elsewhere.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Eva의 집중력(focus)이 다른 곳에 있는 듯했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② focus(집중): 원문 'her focus seemed elsewhere'.
❌ ① energy(에너지): focus와 다른 개념.
❌ ③ talent(재능): 맥락과 다름.
❌ ④ speed(속도): movements가 느린 것은 별개.
det.tip: focus(집중) = concentration. seemed elsewhere = 다른 곳에 있는 듯했다

questions.passage: "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to ①<u>remind</u> you of that." Eva's face softened, as she realized she had been too ②<u>gentle</u> on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is ③<u>doing</u> my best, not being ④<u>perfect</u>."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 자신에게 너무 엄격했다(hard). ② gentle(부드러운)은 hard의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ② gentle → hard: 원문은 'too hard on herself'. gentle은 반대.
❌ ① remind(상기시키다): 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ doing: 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ perfect: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: hard on oneself(자신에게 엄격한)↔gentle(부드러운). remind A of B = A에게 B를 상기시키다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer?"
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"Ms. Blake는 연습 후 Eva에게 조금 더 남아달라고 제안했다."

det.korean: Ms. Blake가 연습 후 Eva에게 더 남아달라고 했다. 원문과 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 'How about staying a little longer?' = 조금 더 남아달라는 제안.
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 F는 틀림.
det.tip: How about ~ing? = ~하는 것은 어때? (제안)

questions.passage: The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played. There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but led the team successfully.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"다음 경기에서 Eva는 여러 골을 넣으며 팀을 이끌었다."

det.korean: Eva는 득점하지 못했지만(didn't score) 팀을 성공적으로 이끌었다. '여러 골을 넣었다'는 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 'didn't score but led successfully'. 골을 넣었다는 것은 틀림.
❌ T: 원문과 반대.
det.tip: didn't score but led = 골은 없었지만 이끌었다. 세부 변조 주의

questions.passage: Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"Eva는 작년 결승전에서 세 골을 넣었던 것을 기억했다."

det.korean: Eva는 세 골을 넣은 경기를 기억했다(recalled). 원문과 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 'recalled the game where she scored three goals'과 일치.
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 F는 틀림.
det.tip: recall = 기억하다. scored three goals = 세 골을 넣다

questions.passage: Eva was worried she couldn't score or pass properly. She was afraid of making mistakes. Ms. Blake suggested that soccer isn't about perfection. Eva's face softened as she realized what truly matters is __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: doing her best rather than being perfect
scoring more goals than the opponent

det.korean: 중요한 것은 완벽해지는 것이 아니라 최선을 다하는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 원문 'What matters is doing my best, not being perfect'과 일치.
❌ ① 이기는 것: 글의 메시지가 아님.
❌ ② 실수하지 않기: 반대. 실수를 두려워하지 말라는 메시지.
❌ ④ 더 많은 골: 글에서 'Not the goals scored'로 부정.
det.tip: What matters is doing my best, not being perfect. 핵심 교훈

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed Eva's slow movements and distracted focus. Eva confessed she was afraid of mistakes. Ms. Blake placed a reassuring hand on her shoulder and told her that what makes her special isn't goals or trophies, but __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: her ability to score more goals than anyone
her perfect technique and flawless performance
her competitive spirit against other teams
the passion and love she has for the game

det.korean: Eva를 특별하게 만드는 것은 경기에 대한 열정과 사랑이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 'It's the love you have for the game' + 'it's about passion'.
❌ ② 더 많은 골: 원문은 'Not the goals scored'로 부정.
❌ ③ 완벽한 기술: 원문은 '완벽할 필요 없다'고 함.
❌ ④ 경쟁심: 원문에 언급 없음.
det.tip: Not A but B = A가 아니라 B. 글의 핵심: 열정 > 완벽

questions.passage: Blake walked along the soccer field after practice. Eva hesitated but agreed. Blake noticed Eva's slow movements. Eva was afraid of making mistakes.

ch: Eva가 먼저 Ms. Blake에게 추가 연습을 요청했다.
Eva는 Ms. Blake의 제안을 즉시 기꺼이 수락했다.

det.korean: Eva는 실수를 두려워했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 원문 'I'm afraid of making mistakes'와 일치.
❌ ① Ms. Blake가 먼저 제안.
❌ ② Eva는 망설인 후 동의(hesitated).
❌ ③ 움직임이 느리고 집중력이 흩어짐.
det.tip: be afraid of ~ing = ~하는 것을 두려워하다. hesitated = 망설였다

questions.passage: The next game, Eva showed new confidence. She didn't score but led the team successfully. She thanked Ms. Blake for believing in her. Eva realized she had been too hard on herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Eva는 코치에게 자신을 믿어줘서 고맙다고 말했다.
Eva는 자신에게 너무 엄격했다는 것을 깨달았다.
다음 경기에서 Eva에게 새로운 자신감이 있었다.

det.korean: Eva는 득점하지 못했다(didn't score). ② '여러 골을 넣었다'는 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ② 불일치: 원문 'didn't score'. 골을 넣었다는 것은 틀림.
✅ ① 일치: new confidence.
❌ ③ 일치: Thanks for believing in me.
❌ ④ 일치: too hard on herself.
det.tip: didn't score but led = 득점은 없었지만 이끌었다. 세부 변조 주의

questions.passage: ① Ms. Blake asked Eva to stay for extra practice after the game. ② Eva hesitated but eventually agreed. ③ Ms. Blake noticed Eva's movements were slow and her focus was elsewhere. ④ Eva recalled scoring three goals in last year's final game.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문의 내용과 다른 문장은?

det.korean: 추가 연습은 경기 후가 아니라 연습 후(after practice). ①은 after the game으로 변조.
det.analysis:
✅ ① after the game → after practice: 원문은 'after practice'. after the game은 다른 시점.
❌ ② 원문 일치: hesitated but agreed.
❌ ③ 원문 일치: slow movements, focus elsewhere.
❌ ④ 원문 일치: scored three goals.
det.tip: after practice(연습 후) vs after the game(경기 후). 시점 변조 주의

questions.passage: (A) Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 문장을 쓰시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)
[ there / was / a / new / confidence / that / hadn't / been / there / before ]
questions.wa: There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before
accept: There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before
there was a new confidence that hadn't been there before
There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before.

det.korean: 이전에는 없었던 새로운 자신감이 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before: 원문 그대로.

questions.passage: Eva's movements were slow and she was afraid of mistakes. In the next game, Eva showed new confidence and led the team. She realized doing her best matters more than being perfect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 축구에서 골을 넣기 위한 기술 훈련의 중요성
코치와 선수 사이의 갈등을 해결하는 방법
완벽주의에서 벗어나 자신의 최선을 다하는 것의 가치
스포츠에서 연습량이 실력 향상에 미치는 영향

det.korean: 주제: 완벽주의에서 벗어나 최선을 다하는 것의 가치.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 글의 핵심: perfection → passion, doing my best > being perfect.
❌ ① 기술 훈련 중심이 아님.
❌ ② 갈등이 아닌 격려.
❌ ④ 연습량이 아닌 마인드셋.
det.tip: What matters is doing my best, not being perfect. 핵심 메시지 = 주제

questions.passage: Blake reminded her that soccer is about passion, not perfection. After their talk, Eva regained confidence and led the team successfully. She realized doing her best is what truly matters.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
With her coach's (A)__________, Eva overcame her fear of (B)__________ and discovered that passion matters more than perfection.

det.korean: 코치의 격려(encouragement)로 Eva는 실수(making mistakes)에 대한 두려움을 극복했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① encouragement — making mistakes: 코치가 격려하고 실수 두려움 극복.
❌ ② criticism(비판): 코치는 비판이 아닌 격려.
❌ ③ losing games: 원문은 실수 두려움.
❌ ④ criticism + losing: 둘 다 틀림.
det.tip: encouragement(격려)↔criticism(비판). fear of making mistakes = 실수에 대한 두려움

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 영어로 완성하시오.
"중요한 것은 최선을 다하는 것이지, 완벽해지는 것이 아니다."
What matters is doing my best, not being __________.

det.korean: 중요한 것은 최선을 다하는 것이지, 완벽해지는(perfect) 것이 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ perfect: 원문 'not being perfect'에서 확인.
det.tip: What matters is ~ing = 중요한 것은 ~하는 것. not being perfect = 완벽해지는 것이 아닌
